title: A restarted app still has the unsent rallies
outcome: Closing the app — or having it reclaimed — no longer discards rallies the server never confirmed. They come back on start-up and go out when the recorder returns to that game, exactly as they would have had the app stayed open.
acceptanceCriteria: The queue is read once when the store's provider mounts. A snapshot whose version does not match is not used rather than migrated, and the store is cleared only when that version is one this build has moved past — a newer one may belong to a build the user is also running.

Stored data that cannot be read, or that carries this build's version in a shape that will not parse, is treated as no stored data and cleared: the app starts with an empty queue instead of failing, and nothing dead is left to be re-read on every start.

Restoring merges into the queue by entry identity with the in-memory copy winning, because the read is asynchronous and the recorder may already have recorded a rally while it was in flight. A rally recorded during the read is never lost.
Restored entries get a fresh attempt schedule rather than the stored one, and are eligible to send immediately when their last failure is one worth retrying.
Whether a restored entry may be retried is decided by the same standard the flush path applies — one threshold, no second predicate and no table mapping error codes to policy.
An empty queue at start-up issues no request at all.
Restoring does not send: nothing is flushed until the recorder opens that game, and the queue may hold entries for more than one game at once.
No screen changes. The indicator, the per-row failure marker and the summary drawer are already projections of the queue and the cache, and become correct by the queue being correct.
The wiring itself is covered, not only the logic: `makeStore()` with no argument reaches localStorage, and mounting the real provider restores a previous run's queue.
